preamble: A long mid front vowel [eː] breaks into a rising or centering diphthong [ia]/[iə]/[ie], typically in stressed syllables. Two independent textbook cases are the Old Irish diphthongization of é to ía before non-palatalized consonants and the Old High German development of Proto-Germanic ē² to ea, ia and finally ie.

examples.note: é (< *ei) breaks to ía before a non-palatalized consonant; PIE *steigʰ-
Compare the genitive dé, where the following palatal quality blocked breaking

examples.to: OHG hiar > Middle High German hier
examples.note: ē² > ea > ia > ie over the 8th and 9th centuries

sources: Thurneysen, R. (1946). A Grammar of Old Irish. Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies.
